lesson.title: Commander au Bistro
lesson.subtitle: Taking a table, ordering with je prends / je voudrais, and asking for l'addition.

hook.title: Ordering at a Paris Bistro: Je prends…, Je voudrais…, and L'addition
hook.content: While English says 'I'll have a coffee / We'll have the soup', French NEVER uses avoir to order food! Instead, French uses prendre ('to take': Je prends un café, Vous prenez le menu ?) alongside polite Je voudrais ('I would like')!

footnotes.title: Why 'J'ai un café' means 'I already have a coffee sitting in front of me'
footnotes.content: To say 'I'll have a coffee', always use Je prends un café or Je voudrais un café!

pattern.title: Order with Je prends / Je voudrais; Close with L'addition, s'il vous plaît
pattern.content: Walk through a complete bistro meal from ordering to paying the check.
pattern.linguist_note: French culinary ordering selects lexical verb prendre ('take') rather than possessive avoir.
pattern.trap_note: Never translate English 'I'll have the soup' with avoir — use Je prends de la soupe / Je voudrais!

exercises.prompt: Match each bistro ordering phrase with its natural English meaning:

matching_pairs.english: Je prends un café (never *J'ai for ordering!)
Pour moi, de la soupe, s'il vous plaît
Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît
matching_pairs.german: A pitcher of tap water, please

exercises.target_answer: I'll have a coffee, What will you have? (waiter asking), For me, some soup, please, A pitcher of tap water, please, The check / bill, please
exercises.meaning: Je prends un café (never *J'ai for ordering!), Qu'est-ce que vous prenez ?, Pour moi, de la soupe, s'il vous plaît, Une carafe d'eau, s'il vous plaît, L'addition, s'il vous plaît
exercises.explanation: prendre is the workhorse verb for ordering food and drink.

exercises.prompt: The waiter asks 'Qu'est-ce que vous prenez ?' How do you say 'I'll have a black coffee, please'?
options: Je prends un café noir, s'il vous plaît
J'ai un café noir, s'il vous plaît
Je fais un café noir, s'il vous plaît
exercises.target_answer: Je prends un café noir, s'il vous plaît
exercises.meaning: I'll have (lit. I take) a black coffee, please
exercises.explanation: French uses Je prends ('I take') for 'I'll have' when ordering.

exercises.prompt: Which English sentences match the waiter's question 'Vous avez choisi ?'?
exercises.meaning: Have you chosen / Are you ready to order?
renderings: Have you decided what you'd like?
traps: Did you pay the bill already?
Do you want to leave the restaurant?
exercises.explanation: choisi is the past participle of choisir ('to choose') — 'Have you chosen?' means 'Are you ready to order?'!

exercises.idea: I'll have some soup and some bread, please (using Je prends)
cues: I take some soup → Je prends de la soupe
and some bread, please → et du pain, s'il vous plaît
idea_parts: verb + fem partitive → Je prends de la soupe
masc partitive + polite tag → et du pain, s'il vous plaît
exercises.target_answer: Je prends de la soupe et du pain, s'il vous plaît
exercises.meaning: I'll have some soup and some bread, please
exercises.explanation: Je prends + de la soupe (f.) + et du pain (m.).

diagnosis.cue: Use Je prends when ordering food and drink.

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.meaning: It was delicious, we would like the bill
exercises.explanation: C'était praises the meal just finished, and nous voudrions l'addition asks for the check.
exercises.affirmation: You combined C'était and nous voudrions l'addition cleanly.

summary.outcome: Order meals and drinks naturally using prendre (Je prends / Vous prenez) and Je voudrais, and ask for l'addition.

use_example.german: Qu'est-ce que tu prends ? — Je prends un café et un croissant.
use_example.english: What are you having? — I'll have a coffee and a croissant.

summary.takeaway: To order food or drink, English 'I'll have' is always French Je prends ('I take').

twist.prompt: Think it through again without looking back — express "I'll have some soup and some bread, please" in French:
twist.target_answer: Je prends de la soupe et du pain, s'il vous plaît
twist.explanation: Re-constructing "Je prends de la soupe et du pain, s'il vous plaît" from the underlying rule cements the pattern of Commander au Bistro.

voudrais.context_phrase: Je voudrais un croissant, s'il vous plaît.
voudrais.context_translation: I would like a croissant, please.
voudrais.etymology_derivation: Future stem voudr- + imparfait ending -ais = the polite conditional!

addition.etymology_derivation: The restaurant bill is literally 'the addition' of the prices.

table.etymology_derivation: Latin tabula 'board, plank'. English borrowed the French word whole — remember it is feminine: la table.

restaurant.etymology_derivation: From restaurer 'to restore' — originally a restoring broth sold in Paris in 1765.

café.etymology_derivation: Turkish kahve → Italian caffè → French café. English took the same journey twice: coffee and café.

vin.context_translation: I would like some red wine.

eau.shift_rule: Latin aqua, all three vowels are ghosts of a
eau.etymology_derivation: Latin aqua → ea → eau: one syllable wearing two vowels and a consonant as historical scar tissue. Feminine: l'eau.

sil_vous_plait.etymology_derivation: 'if it pleases you' — politeness as a small conditional; compare 'if you please', which English still owns.
